projects.name: SURGE
projects.outcome: Turn captured gameplay into replay-backed investigation reports.

steps.label: Play
heading: SURGE STARTS
WITH PLAY.
steps.copy: Survive is a dodging game inside Surge. This replay shows movement from a controlled-speed trial.
facts: 60-second practice round · seed 1337.
Follow the player's path through the arena.

visual.caption: Recorded in Surge
visual.alt: Surge round setup with Controlled speed violation selected and seed 1337

steps.label: Record
heading: SURGE RECORDS
THE SESSION.
steps.copy: Watch Surge receive movement records as the saved trial's data passes through its recorder.
facts: Track game time and received records.
Check for gaps or parse errors.

visual.caption: Recorded in Surge
visual.alt: Surge's Recording view with game time and recording diagnostics

steps.label: Review
heading: SURGE REPLAYS
THE FINDING.
steps.copy: At 20.006 seconds, Surge flags a walking interval. The replay links it to records 689–692.
facts: Surge measured 20.00 cm.
The allowance was 16.17 cm.

visual.caption: Recorded in Surge
visual.alt: Surge replay at 20.006 seconds with the observed distance, allowance, and source record range

steps.label: Explain
heading: SURGE CONNECTS
THE EVIDENCE.
steps.copy: The investigator cites the flagged interval as E1 and records how the measured distance supports the finding.
facts: Read the observation alongside E1.
Reopen the cited moment in replay.

visual.caption: Recorded in Surge
visual.alt: Surge's investigation editor with analyst narrative and attached source evidence

steps.label: Export
heading: SURGE BUILDS
THE REPORT.
steps.copy: Surge exports the saved draft and its cited evidence to a self-contained HTML report.
facts: Review draft revision 3.
The report includes the evidence appendix.

visual.caption: Recorded in Surge
visual.alt: Surge's report export interface showing report readiness and investigation export

projects.name: INSIGHT
projects.outcome: Follow two verified investigations from a question to the bytes behind the decision.

steps.label: Caller
heading: FOLLOW THE
EQUALITY CALL.
steps.copy: Select the plain caller at +0x5D, then follow ready. The highlighted bytes and instruction detail move together as the selection changes.
facts: Case 1 · Insight only
At +0x04, setbe includes equality.

visual.alt: Plain ready routine with the compare instruction and its bytes selected
visual.caption: Recorded in Insight

steps.label: Boundary
heading: CHECK THE
ENCODED BUILD.
steps.copy: Follow the conditional move, compare and equality test. At the eight-second deadline the conditional move preserves C3, so the encoded build also returns ready.

visual.alt: Encoded ready routine with the compare against C3 selected
visual.caption: Recorded in Insight

steps.label: Open
heading: OPEN THE
OBSERVATION.
steps.copy: Open observation.jsonl in Surge. Six records appear. Select the first record, then follow that same saved observation into Insight in the next chapter.
facts: Case 2 · Surge → Insight → Surge
Saved observation · LabCodeProbe

visual.alt: Surge shows observation.jsonl with the first of six records selected.
visual.caption: Recorded in Surge

steps.label: Verify
heading: MATCH THE
CAPTURE.
steps.copy: Open the saved Surge observation in Insight. Verify the supplied DLL to reveal its file bytes alongside the nine captured memory bytes.
facts: Case 2 · Surge → Insight → Surge
LabCodeProbe · RVA 0x1010 · 9/9 readable bytes.

visual.alt: Insight observation window showing identical file and memory bytes
visual.caption: Recorded in Insight

steps.label: Trace
heading: TRACE THE
NINE BYTES.
steps.copy: Inspect the copy, XOR and addition in Insight. Each selection highlights its exact bytes. Save an analyst note that cites the arithmetic instructions.
facts: XOR at 0x1012 · ADD at 0x1015
The match applies to this sample and address range.

visual.alt: LabCodeProbe with the XOR instruction selected in the linked listing and byte view
visual.caption: Recorded in Insight

steps.label: Attach
heading: BRING THE
FINDING BACK.
steps.copy: In Surge, preview the reviewed finding exported from Insight. Attach that revision as E1, then cite E1 in the observations before exporting the report.
facts: The attached revision retains the DLL fingerprint and sampled bytes.
E1 is the first evidence item in this investigation.

visual.alt: Surge shows the pinned E1 Insight finding and its citation in Observations.
visual.caption: Recorded in Surge

steps.label: Report
heading: FOLLOW THE
CITATION.
steps.copy: In the exported Surge report, follow the observation’s E1 citation to the reviewed Insight finding and its supporting evidence.
facts: Recorded from the verified offline report.
The sample establishes byte agreement at capture time. Execution history remains unknown.

visual.alt: E1 evidence appendix in the offline Surge report
visual.caption: Recorded from the exported Surge report

projects.name: STUDYSTEP
projects.outcome: Turn readings into practice, then use the results to choose what to study next.

steps.label: Find
heading: START WITH
A SOURCE.
steps.copy: Search English Wikipedia for a topic, paste your notes, or bring a reading into StudyStep.
facts: Preview an overview before using it.
Import PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown.

visual.caption: StudyStep desktop screens
visual.screenshotAlt: StudyStep’s Wikipedia source preview for Domain Name System.

steps.label: Build
heading: OPEN A
STUDY SET.
steps.copy: The included networking set turns a DNS topic into key points and a recall question.
facts: Import a set or build your own.
Optional local AI drafts material for your review.

visual.caption: StudyStep desktop screens
visual.screenshotAlt: The Networking basics study guide with key points and a DNS recall question.

steps.label: Practice
heading: TRY IT
FROM MEMORY.
steps.copy: What does DNS translate? Try your answer, reveal the reference, then rate how easily you recalled it.
facts: Your rating schedules the next review.

visual.caption: StudyStep desktop screens
visual.screenshotAlt: The DNS flashcard reveals the reference answer and three recall ratings.

steps.label: Adapt
heading: CHOOSE WHAT
COMES NEXT.
steps.copy: After a practice round, StudyStep suggests a topic to revisit. Here, marking DNS as “Needs practice” brings up a guided explanation.
facts: Edit a topic’s assessment or use the results.
Review an explanation, recall, or explain a wrong choice.

visual.caption: StudyStep desktop screens
visual.screenshotAlt: The Next activity panel shows the suggested task and editable topic assessment.

steps.label: Follow
heading: REVIEW SOURCE
CHANGES.
steps.copy: Follow a Wikipedia overview. Open a change, read what was added or removed, and mark it reviewed.
facts: Choose daily, weekly, or 30-day checks.
StudyStep checks while open and catches up on return.

visual.caption: StudyStep desktop screens
visual.screenshotAlt: A weekly check of Domain Name System shows newly added wording and the Mark reviewed button.

steps.label: Read
heading: SAVE THE
NEXT READING.
steps.copy: Explore Wikipedia articles related to a topic in your set. Check why a suggestion fits and what to know first.
facts: Accept a topic to add it to your reading list.
Open the article when you’re ready.

visual.caption: StudyStep desktop screens
visual.screenshotAlt: The reading list shows Multicast DNS, its connection to the study topic, and a link to the article.
